message.content: /deep-research According to data from the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority (https://www.acara.edu.au/reporting/national-report-on-schooling-in-australia/naplan-national-report-archive), for the Australia-wide NAPLAN results for Year 7, which subject had the greatest improvement in average NAPLAN score (when comparing the years 2012 and 2022) and also had a 2022 participation rate equal to or greater than 91%?

input.content:
# Research Plan: Year 7 NAPLAN 2012 vs 2022 Comparison

## Goal
Find which Year 7 NAPLAN subject had the greatest improvement in average score between 2012 and 2022, with 2022 participation rate ≥ 91%.

## Components
1. **2012 Year 7 average scores by subject** - Reading, Writing, Spelling, Grammar & Punctuation, Numeracy
2. **2022 Year 7 average scores by subject** - Same subjects
3. **2022 Year 7 participation rates by subject** - Must be ≥ 91%
4. **Calculate improvements** - Difference between 2022 and 2012 averages per subject
5. **Identify winner** - Subject with max improvement meeting participation threshold

## Constraints
- Data must come from ACARA National Report on Schooling (naplan-national-report-archive)
- Australia-wide (not state/territory specific)
- Year 7 only
- Participation rate for 2022 must be ≥ 91%

## Queries
1. **High depth**: ACARA NAPLAN 2012 national report Year 7 average scores by subject (Reading, Writing, Spelling, Grammar & Punctuation, Numeracy)
2. **High depth**: ACARA NAPLAN 2022 national report Year 7 average scores by subject
3. **High depth**: ACARA NAPLAN 2022 national report Year 7 participation rates by subject
4. **Medium depth**: Verify NAPLAN subject list for Year 7 (confirm 5 subjects tested)
5. **Low depth**: Check if any methodology changes between 2012-2022 affect comparability

tasks.goal: Find ACARA NAPLAN 2012 national report Year 7 average scores by subject (Reading, Writing, Spelling, Grammar & Punctuation, Numeracy). Search the ACARA naplan-national-report-archive for the 2012 report and extract Year 7 mean scale scores for each subject.

tasks.goal: Find ACARA NAPLAN 2022 national report Year 7 participation rates by subject (Reading, Writing, Spelling, Grammar & Punctuation, Numeracy). Extract participation percentages for each subject at Year 7 level.

Based on the research results, I have the data needed to answer the question.

## Summary of Findings

### 2012 Year 7 Mean Scale Scores (Australia)
| Subject | Mean Scale Score |
|---------|------------------|
| Reading | 541.3 |
| Persuasive Writing | 517.9 |
| Spelling | 543.1 |
| Grammar & Punctuation | 545.9 |
| Numeracy | 537.9 |

*Source: 2012 NAPLAN Summary Report (Preliminary), Tables 3a–3e*[1]

### 2022 Year 7 Mean Scale Scores (Australia)
| Subject | Mean Scale Score |
|---------|------------------|
| Reading | 542.6 |
| Writing | 529.8 |
| Numeracy | 546.3 |
| Spelling | Not in PDF (interactive only) |
| Grammar & Punctuation | Not in PDF (interactive only) |

*Source: 2022 NAPLAN National Report PDF*[2]

### 2022 Year 7 Participation Rates (Australia)
| Subject | Participation Rate | ≥ 91%? |
|---------|-------------------|--------|
| Reading | 92.6% | ✅ Yes |
| Writing | 91.9% | ✅ Yes |
| Spelling | 90.7% | ❌ No |
| Grammar & Punctuation | 90.7% | ❌ No |
| Numeracy | 90.1% | ❌ No |

*Source: ACARA NAPLAN 2022 national results dataset (Excel)*[3]

## Calculation of Improvements (2012 → 2022)

Only **Reading** and **Writing** meet the ≥91% participation threshold in 2022:

- **Reading**: 542.6 − 541.3 = **+1.3 points**
- **Writing**: 529.8 − 517.9 = **+11.9 points**

## Answer

**Writing** had the greatest improvement in average NAPLAN score for Year 7 between 2012 and 2022 (+11.9 points), and its 2022 participation rate was 91.9% (≥ 91%).

---
